claims.claim: Unary-count condition iff singleton feasibility iff all partitions feasible; exact Bell/Stirling/pair counts and existing expanded witnesses
Optional explicitly trusted allowedK restricts counts and witnesses, never implicit noK truth information
Actual opposite-label adjacent swap forces coownership in every consistent independent model
True-block connected witness coverage makes graph components actual blocks; trustedK=componentcount yields unique K-compatible ownership

counterexamples: Commutative parity DFAs have no opposite-label swap even with complete behavior and same-K grouping ambiguity
Sparse even/odd unary examples make every partition compatible
Doubled-pair reversals force links missed by adjacent-swap graph
NoK retains all coarsenings even when components equal the actual blocks
limits: Coverage is explicit additional information, not guaranteed from arbitrary passive traces
Prime local factors alone do not certify finite-sample atomicity
Calibration queries belong to separate collector not passive solver
Shared noK witnesses may violate optionalK and must be replaced then
